newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index surges 5.5 pct on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index surges 5.5 pct on rumours.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index surged 5.51 percent on Monday on active speculative buying triggered by rumours that securities regulators were considering market-boosting measures, brokers said.
Officials at Shenzhen Securities Management Office and the China Securities Regulatory Commission declined to comment.
The B share index soared 5.39 points to close at 96.56, with turnover more than doubling to HK$57.79 million from Friday's HK$25.85 million.

Brokers said the surge was linked to a report in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times last Thursday that the China Securities Regulatory Commission had been concerned about the sluggishness of the country's B share markets.

The newspaper quoted CSRC chairman Zhou Daojiong as telling an international business forum in Beijing the bearishness of the B markets had negatively affected China's open and reform policy and major problems in the market included listed firms' transparency, poor results and limited investor base.
The B shares appear undervalued compared to their A share equivalents and a further rise in the market depends on the level of turnover, another broker said.
Vanke was the sharpest gainer on speculative buying, soaring HK$1.98, or 49.50 percent, to HK$5.98 on a single trade of 100 shares, brokers said.
Changan Automobile traded the most on volume of 6.10 million shares and rose HK$0.09 to HK$1.90. Dadonghai advanced HK$0.20 to HK$1.55, with 2.88 million shares traded.
Changchai, the sole loser, fell HK$0.04 to HK$5.01 on trade of 1.07 million shares.
The A share market maintained its upward trend Monday after gains for six straight sessions, with fresh money continuing to flow in, brokers said.

The A share index rose 9.81 points, or 2.29 percent, to a record high of 437.25, with turnover swelling to record 18.20 billion yuan, up from 16.49 billion on Friday. The composite index ended up 9.54 points, or 2.41 percent, at 406.19.
Zhuhai Gree Electrical Appliances Inc, which listed 21 million A shares in Shenzhen on Monday, ended the session at 50.00 yuan per share, making it the highest priced stock listed in mainland China.

The A stock comprises 7.84 million shares issued at one yuan a share between 1989 and 1991, and 13.16 million yuan at 2.50 yuan in 1992. Analysts had expected the issue to stay above 40 yuan today due to the company's strong earnings record.
Chengdu Brilliant Development Group Inc, which listed 18 million A shares and 18 million staff shares in Shenzhen on Monday, closed the session at 20.00 yuan.
The A shares were issued at 9.38 yuan per share via the Shenzhen bourse's automated quotation system last month, while the staff shares were offered at 1.10 yuan per share in 1992.
